questions.q: What does a queue status of ON HOLD mean for a mass addition line?
options: It has already become a posted asset
It is flagged for review and not yet ready to post
It was deleted and will never become an asset
It was merged into another asset
questions.explain: ON HOLD means the line needs further review or missing information before it can be marked ready to post.

questions.q: When should a mass addition line be merged rather than posted as a new asset?
options: When the line represents additional cost on an asset that already exists
When the line represents three physical assets on one invoice
When the invoice was coded to the wrong expense account
When the asset is being retired, not added
questions.explain: A follow-up invoice for additional cost on an existing asset (like an upgrade kit) should be merged into that asset rather than created as a separate one.

questions.q: A $90,000 mass addition line is described as "3 forklifts." What action is needed before posting?
options: Delete the line entirely
Merge it into an existing asset
Split it into three separate lines, each becoming its own asset
Leave it as one $90,000 asset
questions.explain: One invoice line covering multiple physical assets needs to be split so each asset can be posted with its own asset number and cost.

questions.q: Why might the date placed in service need correction during Prepare Mass Additions?
options: Because the GL date from Payables isn't always the date the asset was actually installed and usable
Because mass additions never carry a date
Because Oracle Fusion Assets ignores dates entirely
Because dates can only be set after posting
questions.explain: An asset might be invoiced in one period but not actually placed in service until later, so the GL date from Payables may need to be corrected to the true date placed in service.

questions.q: Why does Prepare Mass Additions exist as a distinct review step rather than posting lines automatically?
options: Because Create Mass Additions is a mechanical process with no judgment about what was actually purchased
Because Oracle Fusion Assets cannot post assets without manager approval
Because every mass addition line is always correct as received
Because tax books require a separate review process from corporate books
questions.explain: Create Mass Additions only follows account coding; a person applying judgment during Prepare Mass Additions catches miscoding, bundling, and category errors before posting.
